info.name: RaderBot
info.description:
The RaderBot API collection is designed for financial software  
developers and traders focusing on automated trading and strategy  
backtesting against the RaderBot application. The source code is located at,

[https://github.com/subaquatic-pierre/raderbot](https://github.com/subaquatic-pierre/raderbot).

It facilitates comprehensive trading operations, including  
strategy initialization, backtesting, and execution, alongside real-time  
access to market data such as klines, trades, and volume.

This is crucial for those aiming to develop or integrate  
sophisticated trading strategies, analyze financial data, and manage  
trading accounts efficiently. RaderBot serves as a pivotal tool for  
enhancing trading bot functionalities and financial software  
capabilities.

item.name: Account

request.description:
Initiates a new trading position based on specified parameters such as  
symbol, margin, leverage, order side, and optional stop loss. This  
request is crucial for entering the market with a defined strategy.

Retrieves comprehensive information about the trading account, including  
dry run status, connected exchange API details, and current positions.  
It's essential for monitoring account status and positions.

request.description:
Configures the account to use specific exchange API settings, including  
exchange name and whether it's operating in dry run mode. This setting  
is vital for integrating the bot with different exchanges and testing  
strategies without financial risk.

Requests the closure of a specific trading position identified by  
position ID. This action is necessary for managing risk and locking in  
profits or cutting losses.

Triggers the closure of all open positions associated with the account.  
This request is a critical risk management tool, enabling rapid exit  
from the market under certain conditions.

item.description:
Contains requests related to account management such as opening  
positions, retrieving account information, and closing positions.

item.name: Strategy

request.description:
Initializes a new trading strategy with specific algorithm parameters,  
including periods for short, medium, and long strategies, symbol,  
margin, leverage, and trading interval. This request is foundational for  
deploying a new trading algorithm under specified market conditions.

Sends a request to stop a specific trading strategy identified by the  
strategy ID. This is crucial for managing trading activities and risk,  
allowing users to halt trading strategies as market conditions change.

Triggers the cessation of all active trading strategies associated with  
the account. This broad action is vital for risk management, enabling a  
rapid response to adverse market situations or when pivoting strategy  
focus.

Allows for the dynamic adjustment of trading parameters for an existing  
strategy, such as the SMA period. This flexibility is key to adapting  
strategies to evolving market analyses and enhancing performance.

Facilitates the modification of a strategy's operational settings,  
including leverage, margin in USD, and the maximum number of open  
orders. This customization is essential for tailoring strategy execution  
to specific risk tolerance and trading objectives.

Retrieves a list of all currently active trading strategies, providing  
insights into the strategy name, parameters, and settings. This overview  
is indispensable for comprehensive strategy management and performance  
monitoring.

Offers detailed information about a specific trading strategy,  
identified by its strategy ID. This detailed view aids in understanding  
the strategy's current state and performance, supporting informed  
decision-making.

Compiles a list of open positions under a particular strategy,  
showcasing how the strategy is currently engaged in the market. This  
request is crucial for tracking the execution and effectiveness of  
trading strategies.

Provides a summary of a strategy's performance, including key metrics  
and outcomes. This summary is valuable for evaluating the strategy's  
success and making adjustments for future trading.

request.description:
Initiates a backtest of a specified trading strategy against historical  
market data. Users must provide a JSON payload containing the strategy's  
name, algorithm parameters (such as period lengths for moving  
averages), the trading symbol (e.g., "BTCUSDT"), margin, leverage, time  
interval for the data, and the start and end timestamps for the  
backtesting period.

item.name: Utils

request.description:
Retrieves the current timestamp from the server. This utility is  
essential for timestamping requests or operations within the trading bot  
environment, ensuring accurate timing for all actions and data logging.

Converts a specific date, provided in year, month, and day format, into a  
corresponding timestamp. This utility facilitates the conversion of  
human-readable dates into machine-readable timestamps, crucial for  
backtesting strategies over specific historical periods.

Calculates the difference in time between two timestamps. This utility  
is useful for determining durations between two events, such as the  
length of time a position has been open or the time elapsed between  
trades.

Given the closing time of a candle (Kline) and the interval, this  
request calculates the opening time of the candle. This is valuable for  
analysis and backtesting, allowing users to align their strategies with  
precise market data points.

Initiates the process of bootstrapping historical Kline data from a  
specified file, symbol, and interval. This utility supports the  
pre-loading of market data essential for strategy backtesting and  
analysis, ensuring strategies have access to historical market  
conditions.

Similar to bootstrapping Kline data, this request bootstraps historical  
trade data for a given symbol from a specified file. It's crucial for  
reconstructing market conditions and testing strategies against actual  
trade executions.

Generates an HMAC signature for a given dataset. This utility is  
critical for enhancing security, particularly when authenticating API  
requests or verifying the integrity of data exchanges within the trading  
environment.

item.name: Market

request.description:
Retrieves the latest ticker information for a specified symbol, such as  
"BTCUSDT". This includes data like the last price, best bid, and best  
ask prices, essential for market analysis and decision-making.

Fetches kline (candlestick) data for a given symbol and interval,  
providing detailed market data over a specified period. This is crucial  
for performing technical analysis and identifying market trends.

Retrieves a list of recent trades for a specified symbol, offering  
insights into market activity and trader sentiment. This data is vital  
for understanding current market dynamics.

Fetches kline data within a specified time range for a given symbol and  
interval. This allows for historical market analysis and strategy  
backtesting over precise periods.

Retrieves trade data within a specified time range for a given symbol.  
This is useful for analyzing market activity and liquidity over specific  
periods.

Provides trade volume data for a given symbol within a specified time  
range, broken down by price granularity. This is valuable for  
understanding volume distribution across different price levels.

Provides trade volume data for a given symbol within a specified time  
range, broken down by price granularity. This is valuable for  
understanding volume distribution across different price levels.

Fetches the last traded price for a given symbol. This information is  
essential for real-time market monitoring and making immediate trading  
decisions.

Initiates a real-time stream of kline data for a specified symbol and  
interval. This enables live tracking of market conditions and is useful  
for dynamic strategy adjustment.

Starts a real-time ticker data stream for a given symbol, providing  
continuous updates on market prices and allowing for timely reactions to  
market movements.

Begins a real-time stream of trade data for a specified symbol, offering  
instant insights into trade executions and market sentiment.

Closes a previously opened real-time data stream, such as a kline,  
ticker, or trade stream. This is necessary for managing data flow and  
resource allocation effectively.

Lists all active real-time data streams, providing an overview of  
currently monitored symbols and data types. This is crucial for managing  
multiple data streams and ensuring relevant market data is continuously  
available.

Retrieves general market information, possibly including available  
symbols, trading pairs, and other relevant data. This is essential for  
understanding the scope of the market and available trading  
opportunities.
